environment.description: Same Laravel 10 application deployed on EKS behind an nginx ingress controller (v1.9.4) configured with mutual TLS authentication via annotation nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/auth-tls-verify-client set to 'on'. The ingress resource specifies auth-tls-secret pointing to a Kubernetes secret containing the CA certificate bundle (namespace/partner-ca-bundle) that includes only the 3 registered partner organization CAs. The auth-tls-verify-depth is set to 2. Connections without a valid client certificate signed by one of the partner CAs receive HTTP 400 from nginx before the request reaches the Laravel application. The ingress also sets auth-tls-error-page to a static 403 page. The TLS termination happens at the ingress controller level, and the backend service is ClusterIP-only (not exposed via NodePort or LoadBalancer), so there is no network path to the application that bypasses the ingress mTLS requirement. Network policies restrict pod-to-pod traffic to only allow ingress from the nginx controller namespace.

config.external_access: only via ingress with valid client cert
